keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Grenada row begins in 1976, nine years after associated statehood (3 March 1967) and two after independence (7 February 1974), so 1967-1975 has no shape. The country is used, which also names Carriacou and Petite Martinique.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 482 km2 against the infobox 344 km2 is a ratio of 1.40 (within a factor of two). The polygon's box (11.99-12.24 N) is the main island only; Carriacou and Petite Martinique (about 12.5 N), which the page names, are outside it. The grid resolves both to the same two cells, so the correction only names the full land.

ledger.note: 3 March 1967: Grenada becomes an associated state of the United Kingdom. 'On 3 March 1967, it was granted full autonomy over its internal affairs as an Associated State'; the West Indies Associated States page gives the same date.

ledger.note: 3 March 1967: the UK keeps external affairs and defence. 'the UK retained responsibility for external affairs and defence'; shown as a client relation until independence; the mapping to a vassal tint is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: 7 February 1974: Grenada becomes independent. 'Independence was granted on 7 February 1974 under the leadership of Eric Gairy, who became the first' prime minister.
7 February 1974: independence under Eric Gairy; same state, same land.

13 March 1979: the New JEWEL Movement overthrows Gairy and sets up the People's Revolutionary Government under Maurice Bishop. 'On 13 March 1979, whilst Gairy was out of the country, the NJM launched a bloodless coup which removed Gairy'; same state, same land.

ledger.note: 25 October 1983: the United States and Caribbean forces invade and occupy Grenada. 'The United States and a coalition of Caribbean countries invaded the island nation of Grenada at dawn on 25 October 1983'; the invasion 'resulted in military occupation within a few days'; two companies of Marines landed on Carriacou on 1 November, 'the last military action of the campaign'. Coup of 16 October 1983 (Grenada page): 'Bernard Coard and his wife, Phyllis Coard, backed by the Grenadian Army, led a coup'.

region.text: the island of Grenada and its dependency of Carriacou and Petite Martinique ('two smaller islands')

ledger.note: December 1983: US troops withdraw. The Grenada page says 'When US troops withdrew from Grenada in December 1983', an interim advisory council was appointed. The invasion page adds that 'American forces remained in Grenada after combat operations finished in December as part of Operation Island Breeze' and that Reagan called the mission 'successfully completed' on 3 November, so the end is dated by the Grenada page and kept at confidence 2 (some forces stayed on). Reviewer fix (am-08-k review): was confidence 1 on the invasion page.

wars.name: United States invasion of Grenada
wars.outcome: Austin's military government was deposed; 'the first democratic elections since 1976 were held in December 1984' and won by the New National Party under Herbert Blaize. No land changed hands; the island was occupied (ledger).
wars.note: Began at dawn on 25 October 1983; Carriacou landing 1 November; Reagan announced the mission complete on 3 November. The occupation is carried by the ledger's occupation events, so the zone list is empty.

certainty.note: Island coasts; the maritime boundary with Saint Vincent and the Grenadines in the Grenadines is not given on the pages opened.

notes: Cliopatria begins Grenada in 1976; the dossier starts at the March 1967 associated-state date (as the sibling antigua-and-barbuda does) and adds a 1967-1975 keyframe. The occupation_end of December 1983 is confidence 2 on the Grenada page ('When US troops withdrew from Grenada in December 1983'); the invasion page gives no withdrawal date and says some forces stayed on (Operation Island Breeze). Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire shape (1969-1995) still contains Grenada (both of its grid cells, checked 1966-1995), so eu-11 must release it in 1974. The 1979-1983 People's Revolutionary Government is a regime change of the same state (rename event), not a rebel state. Three pages opened (budget 1-2) for the associated-state, independence and 1983 events.
